components.label: Caller
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Rope facade
components.responsibility: Validate scalar ranges, split weighted tree and join bounded chunks; publish a new balanced root only after a successful edit.

components.label: Bounded leaf chunks
components.responsibility: Store at most B bytes per leaf, splitting on scalar boundaries; retain both byte and scalar length.

components.label: Weighted internal nodes
components.responsibility: Store left scalar weight and total subtree count; subtract left weight only when descending right.

components.label: Weighted split
components.responsibility: Descend by weight, split at a valid scalar boundary, and rebuild only the search path by joining each detached side.

components.label: Height-aware join
components.responsibility: Descend the taller tree's inner spine until heights differ by at most one, link there, and rebalance on the way back; allocate input chunks once.

components.label: AVL repair
components.responsibility: Apply single or double rotations on repaired paths and recompute heights and weights bottom-up.

components.label: Pinned roots
components.responsibility: Validate the range before splitting, keep nodes immutable and publish the new root in one writer transition. A reader pins a root version and reads only from it.

components.label: Chunk reclamation
components.responsibility: Nodes reachable from the replaced root but not from the new one are retired at the new version and freed only after every reader pinned at an older version unpins; path copying leaves a deleted range inside older roots. Freeing m removed characters is O(m) work, accounted separately from O(log n) navigation.

components.label: Caller
components.responsibility: Invoke the documented API and retain returned outcomes.

components.label: Treap facade
components.responsibility: Use in-order position instead of explicit keys; heap priorities choose structure while cached subtree counts select positions.

components.label: Treap chunks
components.responsibility: Each treap node owns a bounded scalar chunk, its stored scalar width, left/right children and a priority drawn once at creation.

components.label: Subtree totals
components.responsibility: Each node stores count = left.count + width + right.count. count(n) returns that field, and repairing a node after a child change reads only its two children's stored subtree counts.

components.label: Position split
components.responsibility: Split by rank using stored subtree counts; inside a chunk, cut at a scalar boundary and give both pieces that node's priority so each output keeps heap order.

components.label: Priority merge
components.responsibility: Inputs represent consecutive text ranges. Select the lower-priority root and recursively merge only its touching child; repair subtree counts from the children's stored counts.

components.label: Range splice
components.responsibility: Insert splits once and merges input; delete splits twice and merges survivors. Read follows stored subtree ranks without changing root.

components.label: Root publication
components.responsibility: Path-copy changed nodes, publish the new immutable root under a single-writer version check, and retire replaced nodes only after readers pinned at older versions unpin.

components.label: Height guard
components.responsibility: Track depth against a declared guard; rebuild with fresh priorities or reject the operation with old root intact. This is a fallback policy with explicit linear rebuild cost.

requirements.text: Read, insert and delete preserve sequence order with checked half-open ranges and scalar indices.
Maintain subtree sizes and the chosen balance invariant after splits and joins.
Account for inserted bytes, removed-node reclamation, snapshots and invalid ranges without promising impossible O(log n) total copying.

problem.scope: Authored local data-structure study. Compare a height-balanced chunk rope with a randomized implicit treap. Positions count Unicode scalar values, not bytes or grapheme clusters. Insertion of m new characters costs at least O(m); deletion that frees m characters may also cost O(m). Sub-linear targets apply to indexed navigation and structural splicing, not input copying or reclamation.

evidence.testName: batch-07 rope avl: balanced split and splice match scalar arrays

acceptanceCases.given: A rope of a😀bcdef in two-scalar chunks and a rope edited by 300 seeded inserts and deletes.
acceptanceCases.then: Flattened text matches the scalar-array oracle after every edit; cached counts and heights are exact; every node satisfies the AVL bound.
acceptanceCases.when: Split at every boundary, splice Ω🚀 over every legal range, and compare each random edit with a scalar array.

evidence.testName: batch-07 rope avl: balanced split and splice match scalar arrays

acceptanceCases.then: The tree stays AVL-balanced with height at most 12 instead of degenerating into a 256-node path.
acceptanceCases.when: Insert one scalar at index 0, 256 times.

evidence.testName: batch-07 rope avl: pinned snapshots defer reclamation

acceptanceCases.given: A pinned snapshot of abcdefghijkl, empty text, zero-length edits, end insertion and out-of-range edits.
acceptanceCases.then: The pinned snapshot still reads the old text and nothing is freed until it unpins; afterwards the retired nodes are freed while the current root stays readable; invalid edits throw RangeError and publish no version.
acceptanceCases.when: Delete a middle range, read through the pinned snapshot, unpin it, then attempt the invalid edits.

guarantees: Navigation and path repair are O(log chunkCount) with enforced AVL balance; input copying and reclamation costs are additional and deferred past pinned readers.
